Use sliding window for lossless internal pixel buffers

Replace full-height dec->pixels allocations with a sliding row
window bounded by the maximum VP8L backward-reference distance
and copy length. The partial trailing row of that distance lies in
the row being decoded, so the retained history is max_dist / width
rows.

Change-Id: I399190a7c195abc2c506ea53febca5db770a317f

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.

Backward-reference distances are specified in absolute pixels. Once a
window has been shifted, src - data is only the offset into the retained
rows, so compare GetAbsoluteOffset() instead; the window keeps every row
a maximum-distance reference can still touch.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: ae267d8 floors GetMaxDistanceRows to max_dist/width. At width 256 that keeps 136 fewer pixels than LZ77_WINDOW_SIZE, but the backward-reference check is still window-relative (src - data < dist), so a reference that would start before the retained rows is rejected as a bitstream error and CopyBlock32b is never called. dbfb84c changes that check, in both DecodeImageData and DecodeAlphaData, to GetAbsoluteOffset(), i.e. the full-image pixel index. While the row count is still the ceiling, the tightest shift (column 0, immediately after ProcessRows sets last_row) retains ceil(LZ77_WINDOW_SIZE/width)*width = LZ77_WINDOW_SIZE+120 pixels, so every distance the format can encode still lands inside dec->pixels. Together, a length-4095 reference of distance LZ77_WINDOW_SIZE at row 8256 column 0 passes the absolute check and memcpy reads 136 pixels (544 bytes) before the dec->pixels allocation. Each diff is safe against the tree it was written on: the floor is still guarded by the old check, and the absolute check is in-bounds under the old ceiling. Restoring only the ceiling re-creates the surplus the absolute check assumes; restoring only the window-relative comparison rejects the reference before the copy. The overflow is therefore only reachable from the composition, and the repair has to reconcile the row count in the earlier commit with the comparison introduced in the later one.
